sections.h2: Where is Ada County, Idaho, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Ada County sits in southwest Idaho and holds Boise, the state capital and county seat. Wikipedia reports a total area of 1,060 square miles, of which 1,053 is land, with the Boise River running through the northern part and the Snake River forming the southwestern edge.

The Idaho Territory legislature created the county on December 22, 1864, splitting it from Boise County. It is named for Ada Riggs, the daughter of a legislator who helped found Boise. Canyon County was later carved out of its western side in 1891.

Six cities sit inside the county: Boise, Eagle, Garden City, Kuna, Meridian and Star. Hidden Springs and Avimor are census-designated places. Four public school districts serve residents: Boise, Kuna Joint, Melba Joint and West Ada (Meridian Joint School District 2). Homeowners also pay into the College of Western Idaho taxing zone. For a seller, the district and city a house falls in decide which levies appear on the bill.

Interstate 84 and Interstate 184 carry most through traffic, along with US 20, 26 and 30 and several state highways. County roads and highways are maintained by the Ada County Highway District, a separate body from the county government.

sections.h2: What does the Ada County economy look like?
sections.html:
Ada County's job base is anchored by health care, semiconductors, higher education and public schools. The Idaho Department of Labor puts the 2025 county population at 546,141 and the 2024 median household income at $91,502, with a May 2026 unemployment rate of 3.4%.

sections.h2: How does the Ada County Assessor value a house?
sections.html:
The Assessor must place a current market value on every taxable property each year, and Idaho law ties that value to the market as of January 1. Ada County says the appraisal looks at construction costs and recent sales, and may involve a visit to the property.

Notices for the primary assessment roll go out no later than the first Monday of June. Property that missed the primary roll is assessed on the subsequent roll, with notices no later than the fourth Monday in November. Anything still unassessed is picked up by the first Monday in January of the following year.

You can pull your notice from the Assessor's online property records. If you plan to sell, read it closely before you list or accept an offer. Wrong square footage, a missing bathroom or a garage that is really a carport are errors the office can correct, and a correct record makes the property easier to price. For official forms and contacts, start at the Ada County Assessor's appeals page.

sections.h2: How do you appeal an Ada County assessment?
sections.html:
File the appeal form with the Ada County Commissioner's Office on or before the fourth Monday of June at 5:00 p.m. The Commissioners sit as the Board of Equalization, and the office schedules your hearing.

  • Forms are online or at the Assessor's Office, 190 East Front Street, Suite 107, or at the Commissioner's Office, 200 W. Front Street, 3rd Floor, Boise.
  • The appeal addresses market value only. The county says it is not a forum to protest the amount of tax.
  • Bring five copies of your documentation: the original, one for each Commissioner and one for the Assessor.
  • List a contact person on the form so the county can reach you or your representative.

Before filing, the county encourages owners to talk with the deputy assessor who handled the property and to submit market information such as a Realtor's comparative market analysis, an independent appraisal or repair estimates. Values are sometimes adjusted at that stage.

The standard is demanding. The county quotes the rule that the assessor's value is presumed correct and that the taxpayer must show by clear and convincing evidence that relief is warranted. In practice that means sales data from the market, not opinion. The deadline falls in June, so a house that changes hands in spring should have the appeal question settled in the sale agreement.

sections.h2: When are Ada County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The first installment, or the full year, is due December 20. The second installment is due June 20 of the following year. The treasurer notes that the first installment of 2026 taxes is due by December 21, 2026, because December 20 falls on a Sunday.

DateWhat happens
January 1Market value is set; first day to apply for the homeowner's exemption or Circuit Breaker
First Monday in JuneAssessment notices mailed
June 20Last day to pay the prior year's second half without late charge
Fourth Monday in JuneLast day to file an assessment appeal
Fourth Monday in NovemberPrimary roll tax bills mailed
December 20Full-year payment or first half due

Source: Ada County Treasurer, important tax dates.

Miss a deadline and a 2% late charge is added, plus interest at 1% per month starting January 1 after the due date. When the 20th falls on a weekend or holiday, a payment postmarked on or before the 20th is timely the next business day. Delinquent notices for unpaid first-half taxes go out in January, and notices for unpaid second-half taxes go out in July.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill when an Ada County house changes hands?
sections.html:
Ada County bills an ownership change through a separate "missed" roll mailed in February, covering the assessment from the date of the change to December 31. That bill can surprise a buyer or seller who assumed the regular December bill covered everything.

New or finished improvements are handled on the subsequent, or occupancy, roll. Those bills are typically mailed in January and are due in June. A seller who finished an addition or a new build late in the year should expect one.

Ask the title company to pull the current balance and to check for any missed-roll or subsequent-roll bill before closing day. The Treasurer's Office answers questions at 208-287-6800 and posts bills and payment history on its online payment site. You can also reach the Treasurer through the Ada County Treasurer's Office page.

sections.h2: Which exemptions matter when you sell an Ada County home?
sections.html:
The main one is the homeowner's exemption, which cuts the taxable value of an owner-occupied primary home and up to one acre of land by 50%, to a maximum set by the state. The Idaho State Tax Commission lists the maximum as $125,000 for 2021 through 2025, and says it lasts until ownership changes or the home stops being your primary residence. A buyer therefore generally has to apply again.

  • Homeowner's exemption: applied for through the county Assessor.
  • Property Tax Reduction (Circuit Breaker): income-based, applied for through the Assessor.
  • Reduction for 100% disabled veterans: also an Assessor application.

The state tax commission's homeowner's exemption page explains the calculation with an example.

sections.h2: What do Ada County sellers with back taxes usually face?
sections.html:
Sellers who owe back property tax in Ada County face a growing balance, because the 1% monthly interest runs on both the tax and the late charge from January 1. Inherited homes, rentals and houses with deferred repairs often reach this point when no one is watching the mail.

A cash sale can shorten the path from a delinquent notice to a payoff, since there is no lender underwriting to wait on. We buy the house as is, so repairs do not need to happen first. Any unpaid tax is settled through escrow, and the title company will give you an exact figure.

Call or text us for a written offer on an Ada County house. If the offer does not suit you, you owe us nothing.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Ada County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay through the Ada County Treasurer, either online on the county's payment site or by mail. Bills and payment history are available online, and the office can be reached at 208-287-6800.

faqs.q: What is the Ada County property tax appeal deadline?
faqs.a: The deadline is 5:00 p.m. on the fourth Monday of June, filed with the Commissioner's Office. The appeal covers value only, not the tax amount.

faqs.q: Is the 2026 first installment due on December 20?
faqs.a: No. The Ada County Treasurer states that the first installment of 2026 taxes is due by December 21, 2026, since December 20 is a Sunday.

faqs.q: Does the homeowner's exemption move to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. The state says the exemption lasts until ownership changes or the home stops being your primary residence, so the new owner applies on their own.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Ada County house if I owe back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance, including the 2% late charge and monthly interest, is paid from the sale proceeds at closing. Ask the title company for a payoff figure before you accept an offer.
